answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The system stays honest because reputation is unforgeable and only earned through accepted attestations, so freshly minted aliases genuinely cannot swing a verdict. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a ember as the anchor of the cost.
